transcript:
Meeting header: 2026-05-20 15:00 UTC | Duration: ~42 minutes
Attendees: Maya Patel (Redwood AE), Jordan Park (Redwood SE), Ethan Ross (Redwood), Carlos Rivera (SummitPay Sr. Backend Eng), Aisha Khan (SummitPay CTO), Leah Wu (SummitPay DevOps)

[00:00] Maya Patel: Hey everyone, thanks for joining, I think we have about 40 minutes, quick intros?
[00:08] Carlos Rivera: yeah hi, Carlos here, I own backend infra at SummitPay, thanks for doing the walkthrough.
[00:12] Aisha Khan: Aisha, CTO, i'll be listening for security and deployment notes.
[00:18] Maya Patel: Great, Jordan and I will run through the SDK quickstarts — Python and TypeScript — auth, env setup, and a short demo of the Console + Optimize suggestions. We'll leave time for Q&A at the end.

[02:05] Jordan Park: Alright first slide, quick note: the SDKs are tiny wrappers over the REST API, pip install redwood-inference, npm i @redwood/inference, or you can call the REST endpoints directly. For auth we typically recommend an API key stored in an env var, REDWOOD_API_KEY, for dev. For prod you should integrate with your vault/KMS.

[03:30] Leah Wu: for env vars, we use HashiVault. Is there native rotation support with Redwood?
[03:40] Jordan Park: We don't rotate keys in your vault for you, but we integrate fine with KMS and you can use short-lived keys from your identity provider. For private deployment we support customer-managed KMS and HSM options.

[05:10] Maya Patel: Quick demo: Python quickstart. Code sample:
- pip install redwood-inference
- export REDWOOD_API_KEY=sk_live_xxx
- from redwood import Client; c = Client(); c.generate("Summarize transaction data")

[06:25] Carlos Rivera: Quick q: the client picks defaults for model and streaming? We want deterministic latency during pilot.
[06:34] Jordan Park: By default it hits our hosted API with a recommended model; you can pin model and enable streaming. For latency guarantees we recommend Dedicated or private with pinned model variants. Hosted is best to iterate fast though.

[08:00] Aisha Khan: For compliance, SOC2 and audit logs — do you expose user-level logs? We need audit trail.
[08:12] Maya Patel: Yes, we have audit logs in the Console, SAML/SSO integration, RBAC. For Private deployments logs can be routed to customer SIEM so they stay in your environment.

[09:45] Jordan Park: Switching to TypeScript quickstart. npm i @redwood/inference, set process.env.REDWOOD_API_KEY, then:
const client = new RedwoodClient();
const res = await client.chat.create({ messages: [...] });
Streaming example uses event listeners or async iterator depending on runtime.

[11:20] Carlos Rivera: Any gotchas with Node streaming in serverless?
[11:30] Jordan Park: In serverless, long-lived streams are tricky. We recommend short bursts or workaround with chunked responses, or use our managed streaming proxy for heavy workloads.

[13:05] Ethan Ross: For throughput: recommend batching on the client or use our SDK batch helpers. Also set the cache/prefix caching for repeated prefixes to reduce token cost.

[14:40] Carlos Rivera: how do we measure token cost? We are sensitive to cost at scale.
[14:48] Maya Patel: Console shows token-level cost breakdowns per route/model, and Optimize gives suggestions for batch sizes and quantization to lower unit costs. We'll share a benchmark sheet with sample tokens per request.

[16:55] Leah Wu: We run in GCP, any region controls?
[17:05] Jordan Park: Yes, hosted has regional endpoints and we can pin region for data residency. Dedicated pools can be provisioned in specific regions too. For private, you'll run in your VPC.

[19:30] Aisha Khan: On encryption — data at rest and in transit? KMS?
[19:40] Maya Patel: TLS in transit, AES-256 at rest, and KMS integration for customer-managed keys on Private. For Hosted we manage keys unless you opt for dedicated/private with your KMS.

[21:10] Jordan Park: Back to code: sample Node snippet for streaming mis-typed in recording: "client.chat.steam" haha — should be stream. small transcribe quirk.

[22:40] Carlos Rivera: We want to run a small pilot: 2 engineers, 2 weeks, do you have a recommended checklist?
[22:52] Maya Patel: Yes: 1) create test account and API key, 2) run quickstarts (Python/TS), 3) run a few benchmark tests against your workload, 4) evaluate Console metrics and Optimize suggestions, 5) decide whether to commit to Dedicated. We'll attach a checklist.

[25:00] Jordan Park: Performance guidance: start with a 13B-ish open model — we have verified profiles — enable quantized variant if you need lower cost. For strict latency SLOs consider Dedicated with reserved GPU pools and pinned model.

[27:30] Leah Wu: Any pre-built SDKs for batch embedding pipelines? We do a nightly job that embeds millions of transaction logs.
[27:45] Jordan Park: We support bulk embeddings via batch endpoints and Recommend using our export hooks for asynchronous jobs. Also recommend sharding into smaller payloads to avoid OOM. We'll share a sample Python script.

[29:55] Carlos Rivera: Security review — where do we find your SOC2 docs and pen test reports?
[30:05] Maya Patel: We'll send the security pack and share the link to our compliance page; for deep dives we can set up a security call with our security team.

[32:10] Aisha Khan: About auth in prod, we prefer SSO and short-lived creds. Can Redwood accept OIDC tokens?
[32:20] Jordan Park: Yes, we support federated auth for enterprise customers; in hosted we map SSO to user accounts, and in Private you can use your IdP and short-lived tokens. We'll include the SSO integration guide.

[34:00] Maya Patel: Demo of Console: show cost breakdown per-route, per-token, and Optimize suggestions for batch sizes. Small screen noise: console shows a recommended batch size of 8 for typical transaction summarization.

[35:40] Carlos Rivera: If we go Dedicated, what's the onboarding lead time?
[35:48] Maya Patel: Typical lead time is 2-4 weeks depending on capacity and region; we have express options.

[37:10] Leah Wu: Any specific network requirements for Private?
[37:20] Jordan Park: We'll provide a network whitelist, required ports, and gateway instructions. For air-gapped installs it's a longer process; we have an on-prem package.

[38:40] Aisha Khan: Questions around data residency — we'll need logs kept for 7 years for compliance, is that supported?
[38:50] Maya Patel: For Private/Dedicated you can set retention and log export to your SIEM; hosted has retention options with add-on. We'll confirm retention limits in the security pack.

[40:05] Maya Patel: Alright to recap: we'll send quickstarts (Python + TS), benchmark sheet, security docs, and a pilot checklist. Next call: pilot kickoff after you confirm dev env.
[40:20] Carlos Rivera: sounds good, thanks folks.
[40:25] Aisha Khan: thank you.
[40:30] Maya Patel: Thanks everyone, talk soon.

Notes on transcript quality: occasional mis-transcribed words (steam -> stream, KVCash -> KV cache), some crosstalk and short pauses.
